summary: Myth: you can see the Great Wall of China from space with your own eyes. Fact: from low Earth orbit (about 400 km up, where the International Space Station flies) it is generally NOT visible to the naked eye, and it is certainly not visible from the Moon. The wall is long but narrow, and it is built from stone and earth of a similar colour to the land around it. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said in 2003 he could not see it. NASA astronaut Leroy Chiao photographed it from the ISS in 2004 with a 180 mm lens, but said he could not see it when he took the picture. ESA's Alexander Gerst photographed it in 2018 with an 800 mm lens and said it was next to impossible with the naked eye. A few astronauts (Eugene Cernan, Ed Lu) said it may be visible from lower orbit under very favourable conditions.
audience: Pakistani teens and young adults who enjoy myth-busting and arguing in comments

facts.fact: NASA says the Great Wall is generally not visible to the unaided eye from low Earth orbit, and certainly not from the Moon.
facts.source: NASA: China's Wall Less Great in View from Space

facts.fact: China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said in 2003 that he could not see the Great Wall from orbit.
The wall is very long but only a few metres wide, and its materials are a similar colour to the surrounding land, which makes it very hard to see from orbit.
The International Space Station orbits about 400 km above Earth.
NASA astronaut Leroy Chiao photographed the wall from the ISS in November 2004 using a camera with a 180 mm lens, but said he could not see it with his eyes at the time.
ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst photographed the wall in 2018 with an 800 mm telephoto lens and said it was next to impossible to see with the naked eye.
A few astronauts, such as Eugene Cernan and Ed Lu, said it may be visible from lower orbit only under very favourable conditions.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Artificial structures visible from space; Universe Today

facts.fact: From orbit, city lights at night and large structures such as airports, highways and big reservoirs are much easier to see than the wall.
